title: fix(react): the refused-`data` diagnostic gets a test-only reset, beside its siblings
body:
Fixes #9959

The refused-`data` dev diagnostic (objectui#9571, alias leg objectui#9758) kept its warn-once dedupe `Set` as module state in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` with nothing able to clear it, while every other dev diagnostic in `packages/react/src/utils/` pairs its `Set` with an exported test-only reset. `propsBagDiagnostic.ts` states the consequence in its own reset's docblock: the second test to assert the same warning reads the first test's dedupe entry and sees silence, "a green run that checked nothing".

The dangerous direction is the ABSENCE assertion. A test asserting this warning did NOT fire for a `type#id` an earlier block already warned for is green whatever the renderer does, and it reports that green as coverage.

## What changed

- **`packages/react/src/utils/refusedDataPropDiagnostic.ts` (new)** — the dedupe `Set`, the emit `reportRefusedDataPropSpread` moved verbatim, and a new `__resetRefusedDataPropWarnings`.
- **`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`** — the block is gone, one import takes its place. Both `__DEV__`-gated call sites are untouched, as are the emitted message bytes and the `type#id` dedupe key.
- **`packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.refusedDataPropWarnReset-9959.test.tsx` (new)** — the pin.
- **`.changeset/9959-refused-data-prop-warn-reset.md`** — `@object-ui/react` patch.

## Route taken: the `utils/` one

The card left the SHAPE of the remedy to the claiming seat and named two: move the diagnostic beside its sibling, or export a double-underscore-prefixed reset from `SchemaRenderer.tsx`. This takes the first.

`index.ts` re-exports `SchemaRenderer.js` with a star, so a reset exported from where the `Set` used to sit becomes a member of this package's published entry — a contract widening, for a test affordance. The `utils/` route adds nothing to the entry: the reset is reached by relative specifier from the suite, exactly as `__resetDroppedPropsBagWarnings` already is. The route never needed a new export from any published entry point, so the fork the dispatch told me to stop on was not reached.

## `Clause-②: no` — re-derived from THIS diff

Four readings over `0d379f571..8054a2a4b`, not copied from the claim:

```
git diff --name-only                       4 files, none of them packages/react/src/index.ts
git diff -- packages/react/src/index.ts    0 lines (the published barrel is untouched)
git diff -- packages/react/package.json    0 lines (the exports map is untouched)
git diff -- .../SchemaRenderer.tsx | grep  0 lines added carrying `export`, 0 removed
grep -c refusedDataPropDiagnostic index.ts 0 (the new module is not named by the barrel)
```

No consumer of `@object-ui/react` can import anything that did not exist before this change.

## The pin, and why it is not "a test that calls the new function"

`SchemaRenderer.refusedDataPropWarnReset-9959.test.tsx` renders ONE `type#id` (`object-map` with id `shared-9959`) across three `it()` blocks, with the reset in `beforeEach`:

| row | what it renders | asserts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | authored `data` on the object arm | the warning fires |
| 2 | the SAME `type#id`, next block | it fires AGAIN |
| 3 | the SAME `type#id`, rows handed down by a HOST | silence — beside a live-channel control at the end of the same block |

Row 2 is the leg that cannot pass without a clearing reset. Row 3 is the shape the card names: its silence means something only because the control that follows it proves the channel could still speak.

## Ablation

Direction predicted in writing before the run. On-disk mutation through `ablation-replace.mjs` (literal anchor, must hit exactly once, both directions verified against the disk and the blob hash — never an editor's exit code); restore is `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` under a trap, proven by an empty `git diff HEAD` and a blob hash equal to the HEAD blob.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | `_warnedRefusedDataPropNodes.clear();` replaced by a comment (export kept, call site kept) | RED: row 1 passes, rows 2 and 3 fail | **exactly that** — `2 failed \| 1 passed (3)`, vitest exit 1 |
| B | restore | GREEN: `3 passed (3)`, exit 0 | **exactly that**, exit 0 |

On-disk evidence for leg A: anchor `x1 -> x0`, replacement `x0 -> x1`, blob `72c5657b0dc7 -> 1d1b1f64a696`. Restore: blob back to `72c5657b0dc7`, equal to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty over the whole tree.

⭐ Row 3's ABSENCE assertion by itself stays GREEN under leg A. That is not a weakness of the pin, it is the defect being pinned — the silence is indistinguishable from a correct reading, which is why the control beside it is what turns the block red.

The pin resolves `../SchemaRenderer` and `../utils/refusedDataPropDiagnostic` by relative specifier, so the module under test is SOURCE. No `dist/` is in the ablation path and no dist preflight applies.

## Gates

Derived by hand from this repo's `package.json` scripts and `.github/workflows/`, because `dispatch-gates.mjs` REFUSES for this repo (it exists only in `objectstack` and says so). Every exit code captured to a file and read back, never through a pipe. Run from the repo root.

| gate | exit |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/` — 91 files, 1135 tests | 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` on the new pin file alone — 3 tests | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build` (dependency closure) | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react exec tsc --noEmit` | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react exec tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react build` (tsc + dist completeness) | 0 |

`check:readme-exports` needs the whole workspace built: its own output names four unjudgeable types in `plugin-calendar`, `plugin-gantt` and `plugin-kanban` ("run `pnpm build` first"), reports 31 packages unbuilt and declares its population COLLAPSED. Nothing it names is in this diff. It is a repo-wide gate CI owns, and this run measured nothing rather than measuring red.

⚠️ The two eslint warnings on the new test file are `react-hooks/immutability` on the probe's capture container. Its neighbour `SchemaRenderer.legacyPropsDataStrip-9758.test.tsx` emits the byte-identical warning at `origin/main`, so this is the package's existing probe idiom, not a class this branch introduces.

**Declared narrowing:** `eslint` ran over the three changed source files rather than the tree, and no repo-wide `pnpm lint` was run. The rule set that judges those files is not type-aware (`eslint.config.js` carries correctness and ratchet rules, no formatting rules and no project service), so nothing in this diff can move the verdict on a file it does not contain: the three files are the entire population whose verdict this diff can change. The tree-wide run is CI's.

`pnpm test` (full suite) was likewise not run locally — the affected package's own suite was, in full, under the shared verify lock.

## Census the card deliberately left NOT MEASURED

⛔ The card does not claim any test in the tree is green for this reason today, and neither does it here. My own reading, with the command, at the merge base `0d379f571`:

```
git grep -n 'NOT passed to the component' -- packages/react/src/__tests__/
```

Three hits in two files. In both, the block that provokes the warning and the block that asserts its absence render DIFFERENT dedupe keys — `object-map#warned` against `object-calendar#quiet`, and `object-map#warned-alias` against `object-calendar#quiet-alias` — and `object-calendar` is on the array arm, which never warns at all. ⇒ no existing test is silently green for this reason. The defect the card filed is the missing guard, and that is what this closes.
